findings.description: pauseWithdraw() mutates the staker's balance (user.amount -= amount; totalStaked -= amount) WITHOUT calling _updatePool() and WITHOUT recomputing user.phUSDDebt / user.stableDebt. Every other balance-mutating path (stake/withdraw/claim) settles via _updatePool() then resets debt; pauseWithdraw is the one path that violates the invariant. After a PARTIAL pauseWithdraw (user.amount stays > 0), the reward debt still encodes the OLD, larger stake. On resumption, _claimRewards computes pending = user.amount*acc/PRECISION - debt with a shrunken user.amount but a debt sized to the old amount, so pending underflows (Solidity 0.8 revert). This bricks the account's normal claim()/withdraw()/stake() paths (all route through _claimRewards) and, once unpaused, the user cannot call pauseWithdraw again (whenPaused) - remaining principal is locked until/unless the contract is re-paused. Recovery only occurs if accPhUSDPerShare/accStablePerShare grow enough that newAmount*accNow >= oldDebt; with APY==0 and rewardBalance==0 the accumulators never advance, making the lockout effectively permanent for that account. Full pauseWithdraw (amount==user.amount) is safe because _claimRewards early-returns on amount==0 and the next stake resets debt.
vulnerableConditionsMet: share balance (user.amount/totalStaked) mutated in pauseWithdraw WITHOUT a prior _updatePool() settle
reward debt NOT reset after the balance change, so a later _claimRewards reads pending against a stale debt
missingMitigations: pauseWithdraw neither settles pending at the old rate nor rebases user.phUSDDebt/stableDebt to the reduced amount
findings.rationale: Pattern's notVulnerableWhen ('_updatePool runs at head of every balance mutation') holds for stake/withdraw/claim but is explicitly broken by pauseWithdraw. The known-issue note ('pauseWithdraw does NOT claim rewards or update pool - by design') covers reward FORFEITURE; it does not appear to anticipate the stale-debt underflow that bricks the normal exit path and can lock principal. Non-obvious consequence -> in scope.

findings.description: rewardPerSecond is recomputed as (rewardBalance * PRECISION) / depletionDuration on every _updatePool() that distributes (line 416), and again in collectReward (line 283) and setDepletionDuration (line 188). Because _updatePool runs at the head of every stake/withdraw/claim, the depletion rate is re-anchored against a FULL depletionDuration on the REMAINING balance at each interaction. The 'Linear Depletion' model therefore never completes in depletionDuration: distribution follows geometric/asymptotic decay and the more frequently the pool is touched, the slower the runway depletes. There is no windowEnd; emissions stretch indefinitely past the intended window.
vulnerableConditionsMet: effective emission window resets on every user interaction (no fixed windowEnd); stable runway never fully depletes in depletionDuration
missingMitigations: rate is not anchored to a fixed schedule; recompute on remaining balance defeats the stated linear-over-depletionDuration intent
findings.rationale: Maps to EMISSION-WINDOW-BOUNDARY (window/retroactivity boundary error). No direct fund loss - stakers eventually receive rewardBalance asymptotically and stable payout is capped by rewardBalance (no insolvency) - so severity is potential-medium (timing/spec deviation, Law 2 faithfulness to the 'Linear Depletion' story). NOTE: lib/phlimbo-ea/CLAUDE.md explicitly describes this as 'the V1 rate-recompute bug' and states PhlimboV2 removes the recompute from _updatePool. It is NOT listed in registered-projects.json knownIssues for phlimbo-ea. Flagged for sanitizer/ledger reconciliation rather than silently dropped (Law 1 recall).

findings.description: _claimRewards performs external calls - phUSD.mint(user, ...) (line 442) and rewardToken.safeTransfer(user, ...) (line 448) - BEFORE the caller updates user.phUSDDebt/stableDebt. The debt is only refreshed AFTER _claimRewards returns (stake line 317-318, withdraw line 355-356, claim line 379-380). Crucially stake(), withdraw() and claim() are NOT nonReentrant (only whenNotPaused), whereas collectReward() IS nonReentrant (line 270) - an inconsistent-guard tell. If rewardToken (or phUSD) has a transfer/mint callback (ERC777 tokensReceived or any hook token), the recipient can re-enter claim() during the safeTransfer: the re-entrant _claimRewards re-reads pending against the still-unupdated debt and pays/mints the same accrual again (double claim of stable + double mint of phUSD).
vulnerableConditionsMet: state changes (debt reset) occur after the external token transfer/mint
no reentrancy guard on the claim-bearing entrypoints (stake/withdraw/claim)
reward token type is not restricted (owner-set external stablecoin)
missingMitigations: debt not updated before the external transfer (no checks-effects-interactions)
findings.rationale: All three pattern vulnerableWhen conditions literally hold. Confidence is medium (not high) because exploitability is gated on the reward token / phUSD exposing a transfer or mint callback - the reward token is owner-configured (expected standard stablecoin from stable-yield-accumulator) and 'weird ERC20' is a documented known-invalid class. Confidence reflects whether the pattern APPLIES, not severity: if it applies the impact is high (reward drain + phUSD over-mint). Parked as a primary finding for validity-checker adjudication with a coded reentrancy PoC.

findings.description: PhlimboEA holds phUSD mint rights and mints rewards on demand: _claimRewards mints pending phUSD = user.amount*accPhUSDPerShare/PRECISION - phUSDDebt (line 440-442). In the normal single path this is correctly bounded (accPhUSDPerShare is written only by _updatePool, folding in exactly timeElapsed*phUSDPerSecond, and phUSDDebt is reset after the claim). However the reentrancy in PATTERN-003 provides a second path that mints for the SAME accrual before phUSDDebt is updated, over-minting the protocol stablecoin (inflation). This is the pattern's 'two paths can mint for the same accrual (double mint)' condition.
vulnerableConditionsMet: phUSD minted on demand from user-influenceable pending accounting
double-mint path exists for the same accrual via the unguarded reentrant claim (see PATTERN-003)
missingMitigations: phUSDDebt not settled before phUSD.mint() external call
no reentrancy guard on the mint-bearing entrypoints
findings.rationale: Single-path is mitigated (single _updatePool writer + per-claim debt reset + APY emission cap), so the over-mint is contingent on PATTERN-003's reentrancy - confidence medium, cross-referenced. Severity potential-high because over-minting phUSD (the protocol stablecoin) is a direct value/solvency impact. Recorded separately (distinct pattern) but adjudicate jointly with PATTERN-003.

manualReview.description: Two-step APY commit: step1 arms (pendingAPYBps/pendingAPYBlockNumber/apySetInProgress), step2 commits if same bps within the window (block.number > pendingAPYBlockNumber + 100 -> treated as preview). The committed value is the step-2 bps with an equality check against the step-1 snapshot (bps != pendingAPYBps), and the commit branch settles accrual via _updatePool() at the OLD rate before applying the new APY (line 165) - both notVulnerableWhen conditions hold. Caveats kept for review: (a) there is NO minimum block gap - both steps can execute in the SAME block/transaction (isPreview evaluates false when apySetInProgress && bps==pending && block.number==pendingAPYBlockNumber), weakening the two-step as a fat-finger / observation guard; (b) the +100 window is inclusive (commit allowed at exactly +100 blocks); (c) setDesiredAPY is onlyOwner so there is no third-party re-arm/grief vector.
manualReview.rationale: Mostly matches notVulnerableWhen (snapshot equality + settle-before-apply). Same-block commit is a weakening of the intended safety but the story only requires 'two calls within 100 blocks'. QA-grade; parked for human/spec review (Law 2 faithfulness to the two-step intent).

manualReview.description: phUSDPerSecond = (totalStaked * desiredAPYBps) / 10000 / SECONDS_PER_YEAR is a multiply followed by two chained integer divisions (floor). For very small totalStaked (near MINIMUM_STAKE=1e15) combined with a low APY, the per-second emission can floor to 0, silently zeroing phUSD emissions despite a non-zero configured APY. Not strict div-before-mul (the multiply precedes the divides), but the compounded flooring is a precision concern. All other reward math (rewardPerSecond, accPerShare, debt) multiplies by PRECISION before dividing, so precision is preserved there.
manualReview.rationale: Rounding-down favors the protocol and only bites at extreme small-stake/low-APY corners; QA-grade. Parked for completeness.

manualReview.description: emergencyTransfer(recipient) is onlyOwner and moves ALL phUSD (including staked user principal) and ALL rewardToken to an owner-chosen recipient, then pauses. After it runs, pauseWithdraw (the user escape hatch) reverts because the contract holds no phUSD to transfer. 'Malicious owner rug' is out of scope (Law 3, owner trusted). Parked as a visibility note: the interaction where the owner's emergency action drains the very balance the user escape hatch depends on is a potential operational footgun, though it is largely an obvious consequence of 'move all tokens' (design decision: 'Emergency transfer pauses contract and moves all tokens to recipient').
manualReview.rationale: Pattern note says C4 treats centralization as Low/QA unless rug. Leans owner-trust/obvious -> likely suppress per Law 3, but parked visibly rather than dropped (Law 1 recall).

manualReview.description: Empty-pool special handling matched (if (totalStaked == 0) at lines 394 and 462). However the classic first-depositor / ERC4626 share-inflation does NOT apply: staking is 1:1 (user.amount tracks raw phUSD wei, there is NO share-price / exchange-rate math and no donate-to-inflate vector), and a MINIMUM_STAKE = 1e15 floor is enforced on stake (line 296). ERC4626-INFLATION is likewise N/A (no deposit(assets,receiver), no shares = assets*totalSupply/totalAssets).
manualReview.rationale: Signature matched, mitigations present (MINIMUM_STAKE + 1:1 accounting). Not vulnerable; recorded as checked-and-cleared for recall/audit-trail, not as an actionable finding.

manualReview.description: Stable distribution caps toDistribute at rewardBalance (line 406, 'potentialReward > rewardBalance ? rewardBalance : potentialReward') and accStablePerShare advances only by the capped amount, so stable payouts cannot exceed the funded budget (no insolvency for stable). This is a SILENT cap rather than a _safePay revert (pattern's notVulnerableWhen prefers revert-on-shortfall), and combined with the per-interaction rate recompute (PATTERN-002) the runway is asymptotic. phUSD has no funded budget at all (minted on demand, APY-bounded), so the runway concept does not apply to phUSD. No over-pay path found absent the reentrancy (PATTERN-003).
manualReview.rationale: No insolvency (capped distribution). Parked for visibility because the silent-cap behavior and asymptotic runway interact with PATTERN-002; not an independent actionable finding.
